I made a convex inspired reactive web platform:
serverless deployment
scale to zero cost
zero depedencies
tiny frontend bundle
very performant
excellent ergonomics
handles both front end and backend reactivity
Designed to deploy your app on google cloud run + serverless postgres such as planetscale or neon, but easy to adapt.

https://github.com/GW-Jack/concave
nice! is it ok if I include it in #show and tell > community showcase in 0.1.0 blog post ?

Jack Scully Looks pretty cool. I like the one-binary concept.

What's a good app to write on top of this? I see that the README has a chat app. I 'll throw out the challenge to write a better chat app than https://github.com/showell/roc-chat/. It's UPL, so steal away. Are there any other apps you have in mind? I've been wanting to build something that's not chat haha.
Cool! Is it possible to use with Roc-based frontend frameworks like Joy or roc-signals?

@Steve Howell The chat app is a good idea. The example project is a chat app, but I'm not invested in making it good from a product perspective. I think doing a port of roc_chat would be a nice way to compare and contrast approaches.

@notramo It has a build in lightweight frontend framework that gives reactive components. I didn't write it for general frontend framework compatibility.

You can check out the framework in the docs/CLIENT_SDK.md
So it's only usable in JavaScript frontends?

I'm not sure if you are asking if concave targets native mobile and desktop apps, or if you are asking whether you write frontend code as a javascript file.

You write the frontend code as a plain javascript file.
It does not target desktop or mobile apps without a wrapper like tauri or electron
Joy and roc-signals are running Roc in the browser.
WASM, with a small JS bridge for DOM modifications.

You write the frontend code as a plain javascript file.

Based on this, I guess, concave is not compatible with these frameworks.
